title: Ellington's brief open solo spaces
summary: Duke's arrangements left a bare space marked 'solo' of eight or sixteen bars, with no time to settle in on an original tune.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Duke, on the other hand, Duke would write arrangements like that and it'll have an open space and just say, "Solo." Now, that's an original tune. What are you going to

solo if you don't hear it? What's going on, you know? And then there will be about eight bars or 16 bars and that's it. Then, probably just about the time you're getting used to what you're hearing, you're off, your solo's gone. See, that's the difference.
